1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module thirteen: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Time and format. The routine for every question. Checklists. Pairs the exam likes to confuse. Common traps. The final week. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: Both skill areas. Exam format: a score of seven hundred on a scale of one to one thousand passes; check the exam page for the time. Validated against: the official A I nine oh one study guide, current skills measured.

1.title: Time and format
1.text: Time and format. The duration and the number of questions are not given on the pages this course was built from, so check the exam page and divide the time by the number of questions. First pass. Answer what you know quickly; mark the rest. Second pass. Return to marked questions. Last minutes. No question left blank.

1.title: The routine for every question
1.text: The routine for every question. Read the last sentence first. Find the key need: text, speech, image, document, agent, safety, cost, settings. Name the workload or the Foundry feature and drop options from other areas. Pick the most specific match. For a code question, read: client, credential, call, input, output. Mark and move on if two options remain after a minute.

1.title: Identify AI concepts and capabilities (40–45%)
1.text: Identify A I concepts and capabilities (forty to forty-five percent). The six principles and a clue for each: fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability. Tokens, transformer and attention, embeddings, context window, no memory between calls, hallucinations, grounding. Model kinds: L L M, S L M, reasoning, multimodal, image generation, embedding. Deployment: Global Standard, Data Zone, provisioned, batch; the catalog's two categories. Parameters: temperature (low focused, high varied), top p, max tokens; reasoning models differ. The six workloads: generative, agentic, text analysis, speech, vision, information extraction. Text techniques: key phrases, entities, sentiment, summarization (extractive versus abstractive), language detection, P I I. Speech: recognition (real-time, fast, batch), synthesis (neural, custom voice, S S M L), translation. Vision: caption, tags, object detection, Read (O C R), people; image generation creates images. Extraction: documents, images, audio, video; extract, classify, generate; confidence and grounding.

1.title: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%)
1.text: Implement A I solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (fifty-five to sixty percent). System versus user prompt; few-shot; ground with source text; "I don't know" rule. Foundry resource, project, endpoint; portal Build to Catalog to Deploy; playground, compare mode. S D K chat client: A I Project Client, Default Azure Credential, get openai client, responses.create(model, input), output text. Agent equals model plus instructions plus tools; prompt, voice and hosted agents; tools (file search, code interpreter, web search, function calling, M C P); conversation keeps history. Text app: Text Analytics Client, analyze sentiment; speech app: Speech Config, Audio Config, Speech Recognizer. Multimodal: user content list with text and image parts; images.generate, base sixty-four result. Content Understanding: analyzers (prebuilt, custom), begin analyze, poller.result().

1.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse
1.text: Pairs the exam likes to confuse. System versus user prompt. developer rules versus the person's question. Generative versus agentic A I. creates content versus uses tools to act toward a goal. Text analysis versus generative A I. facts about existing text versus new text. Speech recognition versus synthesis. audio to text versus text to audio. Analyze an image versus generate an image. understand a picture versus create a picture. Extractive versus abstractive summary. picks sentences versus writes new ones. Extract versus classify versus generate. value as written versus a category versus a written value.

1.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse, continued
1.text: Pairs the exam likes to confuse. Prebuilt versus custom analyzer. common scenarios versus your own fields. Standard versus provisioned versus batch. pay per token versus reserved capacity versus discounted asynchronous. Temperature versus max tokens. randomness versus length. Fairness versus inclusiveness. equal treatment of groups versus usable by everyone. Transparency versus accountability. understandable versus someone responsible. Resource versus project. the Azure container versus your workspace. Real-time versus batch transcription. streaming versus many files later.

1.title: Common traps
1.text: Common traps. "A I nine hundred materials are fine." A I nine hundred was retired on June thirty, two thousand twenty-six. "The model remembers earlier calls." It has no memory; the app resends messages (or uses a conversation). "Higher temperature means more accurate." It means more varied. "Reasoning models accept temperature." They do not. "Tokens are words." Tokens can be sub-words. "Images go in the system prompt." An image goes in the user message as an image part. "A confidence score of one is guaranteed." It is an estimate of reliability. "Old names." Azure A I Foundry is now Microsoft Foundry; Azure A I Services is now Foundry Tools.

1.title: The final week
1.text: The final week. seven to five. One module per day with its card; answer recall questions from memory. four to three. Read the sample programs again line by line; do the pairs and traps out loud. two. Redo all practice questions; list your misses. one. Light review; check the exam time, I D and rules; rest.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors wants its support bot to stay on topic and polite. Where do the rules belong? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: In the system prompt. The system prompt sets the standing role, scope and tone.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. Which principle applies when a loan model treats two groups differently for no good reason? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Fairness. Unequal treatment of groups is a fairness issue.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. What counts both the prompt and the response against a limit? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: The context window. The context window is measured in tokens for prompt plus response.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team needs creative, varied slogans. Which change helps? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Raise the temperature. Higher temperature makes answers more varied.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. An assistant must look up an order and then update a ticket by calling systems. Which approach fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: An agent with action tools. Agents use tools to take actions.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. Which call creates an image from a description? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: images.generate. Image generation uses the images.generate call.

1.title: Practice Question 7
1.text: Question seven. Which tool extracts fields from invoices and returns a confidence score for each? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Azure Content Understanding. Content Understanding extracts fields and returns confidence scores.

1.title: Practice Question 8
1.text: Question eight. A Python program needs to authenticate to a Foundry project without a key in the code. What does it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Default Azure Credential. Default Azure Credential uses the signed-in Microsoft Entra I D identity.

1.title: Practice Question 9
1.text: Question nine. Which speech object states whether audio comes from the microphone or a file? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Audio Config. Audio Config defines the audio source.

1.title: Practice Question 10
1.text: Question ten. Which deployment type should most workloads start with? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: Global Standard. The documentation advises starting with Global Standard.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. Name the six responsible A I principles. Answer: Fairness, reliability and safety, privacy and security, inclusiveness, transparency, accountability. Question two. What are the three parts of an agent? Answer: Model, instructions and tools. Question three. Which method creates an agent version? Answer: project.agents.create version.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What does begin analyze return? Answer: A poller; call result() to get the analysis. Question five. Which exam replaced A I nine hundred? Answer: A I nine oh one. Question six. What do you read first in a question? Answer: The last sentence.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. Exam: A I nine oh one; pass at seven hundred; concepts forty to forty-five percent, Foundry implementation fifty-five to sixty percent; A I nine hundred retired. Method: last sentence, key need, name the workload or feature, most specific match. Biggest confusions: system versus user; generative versus agentic; extract versus classify versus generate. Traps: no memory, temperature is variety not accuracy, tokens are not words, reasoning models ignore temperature, old product names. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
